raw.core_excitement: The founder is excited about enabling a "Continuous AI lift" for AI-first companies by building a system that can observe work, decide what AI should do, and then automatically build and deploy AI agents for those tasks.
raw.thesis: narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" for AI-first companies. It observes work patterns through desktop sensors (Layer 1), analyzes employee intent, task value, and workflow "drift" using an "Intelligence Layer" (Layer 2), and then automatically generates, deploys, and monitors AI agents for high-ROI opportunities via an "Agent Factory" (Layer 3). This venture leverages existing foundation models, focusing its innovation on understanding the "Work Graph" to identify inefficiencies and strategically inject AI assistance into workflows. The core value proposition is to enable continuous AI-driven improvement by automating the detection, validation, and deployment of AI agents within AI-first organizations, thus allowing them to "see, prove, and deploy AI automation at scale." This venture is targeting growth, aiming to provide a comprehensive system for AI orchestration and optimization. It appears to be at the idea stage, as no concrete evidence of a built product or users is provided in the intake form. The venture effectively replaces or significantly augments existing methods of process analysis and AI deployment by integrating observation, intelligence, and automated agent creation into a single, continuous system.
raw.product_description: narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" with three layers: an "Observe" layer (Lightweight desktop sensors capture work patterns), an "Intelligence Layer" (a "Brain" that detects employee intent, business value of tasks, and workflow "drift"), and an "Execution Layer" (an "Agent Factory" that generates, deploys, and monitors AI agents for high-ROI opportunities). It uses existing foundation models and focuses on the "Work Graph" to optimize AI intervention.
